meta.name: Lapaas AI Product Engineering: verified course knowledge base
meta.prepared_by: Himanshu Bartwal, prototype for the Lapaas internship assignment. Not an official Lapaas document.
meta.rules: Answers quote or closely paraphrase the official course page. Entries with status not_stated cover questions the page does not answer; the assistant must say it cannot verify them and suggest the Lapaas team.

entries.question: What is the Lapaas AI Product Engineering course?
entries.answer: It’s a self-paced online course by Lapaas that helps you go “from a rough AI idea to a working, deployed product”. You learn product research, AI-assisted full-stack development, multimodal workflows, RAG, MCP, agents, automation and launch “through a framework tested live with students, now available at your pace.” Your mentor is Sahil Khanna.

entries.question: Who is this course for?
entries.answer: The page names three audiences: students & freshers (“Graduate with proof, not just marks.”), business owners (“Run leaner with AI-augmented systems.”) and marketers & freelancers (“Sell useful outcomes, not more hours.”). It says the course is for you if “You want to build and publish, can commit a few focused hours each week, and prefer practical systems over AI hype.”

entries.question: I’m a working professional. Is this course for me?
entries.answer: Working professionals are not named as a separate audience on the page (it names students & freshers, business owners, and marketers & freelancers). The curriculum is the same for everyone. One problem the page lists is “Worried your role will shrink”: “You can see routine work being automated but do not yet know how to move up the value chain.” The page says the course suits people who “can commit a few focused hours each week”.

entries.question: Who should NOT take this course?
entries.answer: The page says it’s “not for everyone”. It is not for you if you want a magic prompt, cannot commit focused time, only want videos to binge, want theory without shipping, or will not show your work. In its words: “The self-paced course provides structure, examples, projects and community access. You still provide the attention, practice and willingness to publish imperfect work.”

entries.question: Do I need coding experience?
entries.answer: You can start without knowing coding. The page says: “Yes. The course starts with AI, product and development foundations before moving into full-stack apps, RAG, MCP, agents and production. You should still expect to practise and build alongside the lessons.” You can also contact Sahil and ask questions in the Lapaas learner community while you learn.

entries.question: What does the course cover?
entries.answer: Nine areas: AI & Product Foundations · Product Thinking & PRDs · AI-Assisted Development · Full-Stack MVP Engineering · Multimodal AI · RAG & Knowledge Layers · MCP, APIs & Integrations · Agents & Automation · Production, Launch & Growth. They follow four stages: Discover, Build, Connect and Ship. The first area is where you “Understand models, tokens, context and cost”.

entries.question: What will I have built by the end?
entries.answer: The course path has four stages, each with a deliverable named on the page: Discover → “A validated product brief + prototype”; Build → “A tested, data-backed MVP”; Connect → “A grounded, tool-using AI workflow”; Ship → “A deployed product + improvement plan”. The FAQ says you learn “the workflow behind full-stack AI products, data-backed applications, multimodal experiences, RAG knowledge layers, MCP integrations, agents, automations and deployable product systems.”

entries.question: What do I finish the course with?
entries.answer: The page says “Finish with assets. Not just information.” You finish with: a portfolio of working AI products; a portfolio people can inspect (demos, architecture thinking, project decisions and case studies); commercially useful skills (“A path from audit to pilot to retainer, grounded in real Indian business problems.”); and a reusable builder system for future projects.

entries.question: How does this help students and freshers?
entries.answer: For students & freshers the page says “Graduate with proof, not just marks.” and lists four things: “Build a portfolio of working AI products”, “Understand the stack behind AI job descriptions”, “Turn projects into case studies and demos” and “Start freelancing with practical proof”.

entries.question: How does this help business owners?
entries.answer: For business owners the page says “Run leaner with AI-augmented systems.” and lists: “Automate operations, support and reporting”, “Prototype tools before hiring a large team”, “Own workflows instead of stacking SaaS costs” and “Evaluate AI vendors from first principles”. The MCP module covers how to “Connect AI to customer data, analytics, ads, WhatsApp and the tools where real work happens.”

entries.question: How does this help marketers and freelancers?
entries.answer: For marketers & freelancers the page says “Sell useful outcomes, not more hours.” and lists: “Build content and visual AI workflows”, “Automate funnels and client reporting”, “Add AI audits, pilots and automations” and “Create repeatable service IP”. Its commercial path is Audit → Pilot → Working system, and it notes that “commercial results still depend on your execution, market and customer acquisition.”

entries.question: Which tools will I learn?
entries.answer: Tools named on the page include Claude, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Supabase, LangChain, n8n and Gemini, plus GitHub and Postgres, and Vercel, Docker and Coolify for deployment. The page also says: “Tools will keep changing. A strong product-engineering process compounds.”

entries.question: Will the tools become outdated?
entries.answer: The page answers: “Individual tools change quickly. The curriculum connects them to durable ideas: product thinking, context, retrieval, tools, evaluation and deployment. Those are the parts worth learning.”

entries.question: Is this a live course or self-paced?
entries.answer: It’s self-paced. The page says: “No. This is a self-paced online course with no scheduled live classes.” and “This is a self-paced course, not a current live batch.” The framework was first tested with students in a completed cohort; the course includes practical classroom Q&A from that cohort, plus community access to ask Sahil questions.

entries.question: When can I start?
entries.answer: Whenever you’re ready. The page says “Course access starts when you join” and you can “Follow the original curriculum in order without waiting for a class or a new batch.” There are “no scheduled live classes or attendance dates.”

entries.question: How long do I get access, and where?
entries.answer: “You receive 3 months of access in the Edrilla app from activation. During that window you can revisit lessons and use the included files.” Your lessons, slide decks, lab files and assignments are organised inside the Edrilla app.

entries.question: What is the price? Is EMI available?
entries.answer: ₹2,999, one-time payment, GST included, with 3 months access. Checkout is via Razorpay. On EMI the page says: “Eligible cards may show Razorpay EMI options at checkout. The full course price is ₹2,999 including GST.”

entries.question: What’s included when I buy?
entries.answer: The page lists: the complete self-paced course from product foundations through production; practical classroom Q&A from the completed cohort; the Lapaas learner community “where you can contact Sahil and ask questions”; the end-to-end curriculum; practical build patterns; course resources in the Edrilla app; “3 months of access from activation”; and a “Completion certificate after finishing the course requirements”.

entries.question: Can I ask Sahil my doubts?
entries.answer: Yes. “Your purchase includes access to the Lapaas learner community, where you can contact Sahil and ask questions as you work through the course.” The page doesn’t state a response time.

entries.question: Will I get a certificate?
entries.answer: Yes. “Finish the course requirements to receive a Lapaas AI Product Engineering completion certificate.” The page calls it completion-based and “Designed to sit beside the practical work you create”. The exact course requirements are not stated on the page.

entries.question: Is there a money-back guarantee?
entries.answer: The page shows a “30-day money-back guarantee”: “Start the course, work through the opening lessons and test the learning structure. If it is not the right fit, the existing Lapaas refund policy applies within 30 days.” The linked Lapaas refund policy has conditions (for example, a request by email with evidence of active participation and implementation) and doesn’t name this course. I can’t promise a refund, so please read the policy and confirm with the Lapaas team.

entries.question: Who is the mentor?
entries.answer: Sahil Khanna. The page says he has 14 years building businesses and teams and “built a 150-person digital marketing agency, then redesigned it into a lean AI-augmented studio”. It also lists “2,400+ alumni”, a “7-figure AI-augmented studio” and “TED · ET featured speaker”.

entries.question: Are the student reviews about this self-paced course?
entries.answer: The page says: “These reviews refer to the completed live cohort that shaped today’s self-paced course. They are historical student experiences, not a promise of live classes.”

entries.question: Will this course get me a job?
entries.chip: Will it get me a job?
entries.answer: The official page does not promise or guarantee a job, placement or income. What it says for students & freshers: the course helps you “Build a portfolio of working AI products”, “Understand the stack behind AI job descriptions” and “Turn projects into case studies and demos”. It also says “commercial results still depend on your execution, market and customer acquisition.”

entries.question: How much time do I need each week?
entries.answer: “Plan for several hours each week to watch, practise and finish the project work.” The page says the course suits people who “can commit a few focused hours each week”. Access lasts 3 months from activation. The total course length in hours is not stated on the page.

entries.question: Which real products are used in the teaching?
entries.answer: The course teaches through products Sahil built: CallTrack (CRM + automation), Autocut (agentic video), Thumbnail Maker (visual AI), Logoforge (AI product), Solopages (marketplace) and Landing Systems (vibe coding). The page says “These are not invented course exercises. Sahil used the cohort to unpack products he was actually building”. It does not say students build these same products.

entries.question: How can I contact the Lapaas team?
entries.answer: Message the Lapaas team on WhatsApp at +91 95400 65704. The page says: “Need help choosing? Message the Lapaas team and ask a specific question about the AI Product Engineering course.”

entries.question: How many hours or lessons is the course?
entries.answer: Not stated on the official page, so I can’t verify the total hours or number of lessons. What the page does say: “Plan for several hours each week”, and you get 3 months of access. Please ask the Lapaas team on WhatsApp for the exact length.

entries.question: Do I need to pay for tools or API credits?
entries.answer: Not stated on the official page. It names tools like Claude, Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, but doesn’t say whether you need paid subscriptions or API credits to follow along. Please ask the Lapaas team before you buy.

entries.question: Can I watch on my phone and laptop, or on multiple devices?
entries.answer: Not stated on the official page. It only says the course is inside the Edrilla app. Device rules (phone, laptop, how many devices) aren’t mentioned, so please ask the Lapaas team on WhatsApp.

entries.question: Can I extend access after 3 months?
entries.answer: Not stated on the official page. It says you get 3 months of access from activation, but nothing about extending it. Please ask the Lapaas team.

entries.question: Is the course taught in Hindi or English?
entries.answer: Not stated on the official page. It doesn’t say which language the lessons are taught in. Please ask the Lapaas team.

entries.question: Is there a discount or coupon code?
entries.answer: Not stated on the official page. It shows one price: ₹2,999, one-time, GST included. I can’t verify any discount, coupon or scholarship, so please ask the Lapaas team.

entries.question: What do I need to do to get the certificate?
entries.answer: Not stated on the official page. It says you get the certificate after “finishing the course requirements”, but it doesn’t list those requirements. Please ask the Lapaas team.

entries.question: Is there placement support or internship help?
entries.answer: Not stated on the official page. It doesn’t mention placement support, job referrals or internships, and it doesn’t promise a job. Please ask the Lapaas team if this matters to you.

entries.question: Is there a free trial or sample lesson?
entries.answer: Not stated on the official page. It doesn’t mention a free trial or sample lesson. Please ask the Lapaas team.
